tagline.text: An airport city born from an old U.S. air base, with Kapampangan cuisine

location.label: Location
location.text: Clark Freeport Zone, Angeles and Mabalacat, Pampanga Province

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–April (dry season); hot air balloon festival in February

children.text: Once the largest U.S. Air Force base outside America, this city has become a freeport zone of wide lawns and tree-lined avenues, where you can enjoy a direct-flight airport from Korea, resorts and golf courses, and the food of Pampanga, the Philippines' culinary capital, all at once.
Clark is a freeport zone spanning Angeles City and Mabalacat City in Pampanga Province, on the site of Clark Air Base, which stood from
to
. During the Cold War it was one of the largest U.S. military bases outside the mainland United States, but in

the base was buried in ash from the eruption of Mount Pinatubo, and that same year the Philippine Senate refused to extend the base agreement, leading to a U.S. withdrawal. It was later converted into a special economic zone managed by the Clark Development Corporation (CDC), where an airport, industrial parks, resorts, casinos, and golf courses were built.

Traces of the base era remain in many places today. The sprawling lawns of the old parade ground, the straight roads lined with acacia trees, and the low-rise houses and restaurants converted from former officers' quarters create a relaxed atmosphere completely unlike hectic Manila. With little traffic congestion and well-managed security, it's also a city with a large population of retirees, long-term expat families, and Korean residents.
Since opening a new passenger terminal in

, Clark International Airport (CRK) has connected directly with Incheon, Busan, and other Korean cities, making it a gateway for starting a trip to northern Luzon without going through Manila. It's only
10–20 minutes
by car from the airport to a hotel in town, making it easy to start your trip from the day you arrive.

Pampanga, home to Clark, is a region Filipinos themselves call the "culinary capital." Signature Filipino dishes like sisig, tocino, and burong kanin were all born here. You can combine the convenience of an airport city, the history of the base era, Pampanga's food, and side trips to Pinatubo and Subic, making it a great fit for family trips, golf trips, and short weekend getaways alike.

Angeles is the birthplace of sisig, chopped pig's head grilled on a hot plate. Visit the old restaurants considered the originators of sisig and traditional eateries in San Fernando to taste authentic Kapampangan cuisine.
A vast lawn plaza that once served as the base's parade ground, busy at dusk with locals walking, jogging, and picnicking. It's a good spot to explore alongside the surrounding old base buildings.
Lays out Clark's history at a glance, from the Spanish era through the U.S. military base, the eruption of Pinatubo, and the transformation into a freeport zone.
1–1.5 hours
is enough.

children.text: The Philippines' biggest aviation festival, launched in
and held near Clark around
February
each year. The 26th edition in
was held on
February
13–15 in New Clark City, Capas, Tarlac; the venue and dates change each year, so check the announcements.

There are plenty of facilities for spending half a day with the kids, such as Dinosaurs Island, filled with dinosaur models; the Aqua Planet water park; and Sandbox in Porac, with a zipline and rope course.
There are several 18-hole golf courses in and around Clark, drawing many Korean golf travelers. Weekday green fees are cheaper than in Korea, and the short travel distance is a plus.
Walk through the old downtown, home to the Holy Rosary Parish Church built in the late 19th century and the Angeles City Museum, and get a feel for Pampanga's history.

Clark International Airport (CRK) has direct flights with several Korean cities including Incheon and Busan, with a flight time of about
4 hours
. Domestic flights also connect to Cebu, Davao, Boracay (Caticlan), Palawan, and more. Routes and airlines change by season, so check the latest schedule. From the airport to a hotel in Clark, it's
10–20 minutes
by taxi or hotel pickup.
The easiest way from Manila is the airport-connecting P2P bus. Buses (Genesis, etc.) run to Clark International Airport and SM Clark from NAIA Terminal 3, PITX, Trinoma, and Cubao, taking about
2.5–3 hours
, with fares around
. For a cheaper option, take a northbound bus (Victory Liner, etc.) from Cubao or Pasay, get off at the Dau terminal in Mabalacat, and continue into Clark by jeepney or taxi (bus fare about
From Manila, take NLEX north for about
, taking
1.5–2.5 hours
. Toll costs are about
one way. Inside Clark, the roads are wide and uncrowded, making driving easy.
Within Clark, you can use ride-hailing apps like Grab, taxis, or the Clark loop jeepney. In Angeles town, jeepneys and tricycles are the main transport, costing about
for a short ride.
Clark's dry season is
November–April
December–February
has cool mornings and evenings and clear skies, best for outdoor activities, and
February
brings the hot air balloon festival with plenty to see.
March–May
is the hottest stretch of the year, with midday temperatures climbing to around 35°C, so it's best to mix indoor sightseeing with outdoor activities.
June–October
is the wet season, with strong afternoon showers, and
July–September

can see several days of rain in a row due to typhoon effects. If your trip is mostly city sightseeing and food, the wet season isn't too inconvenient, but Pinatubo tours are often suspended during this period.
Year-end in Pampanga is special. At the Giant Lantern Festival in San Fernando, held around
mid-December

, you can see the spectacle of enormous Christmas lanterns (parol) made of thousands of light bulbs twinkling in time with music. During Holy Week, some Pampanga towns hold religious events reenacting actual crucifixions, drawing large crowds.
Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
Accommodation splits broadly into two areas. Inside the Clark Freeport Zone, casino resorts, golf resorts, and international chain hotels cluster together, offering a quiet and safe stay for about
a night. Angeles town and the area around Fields Avenue have many cheap hotels at

a night, but since it's close to the nightlife district, family travelers are better off staying inside Clark proper or near a mall. Long-term stayers sometimes rent serviced apartments or condos by the month.

Food is the heart of a trip to Clark. Aling Lucing, the original sisig restaurant that got its start beside the Angeles railway, has been a thriving landmark for decades. Everybody's Cafe in San Fernando is a long-established restaurant that has served traditional Kapampangan dishes since the

s, where you can try frog dishes, kare-kare, and dishes served with burong kanin. Sweet cured pork tocino, longganisa sausage, and traditional Pampanga sweets turon and sans rival are also popular souvenirs.

Being a city with a large Korean expat community, there are also many Korean restaurants, Korean grocery stores, and Korean-style cafes, which is convenient when you're missing Korean food during a long trip.
When you arrive at Clark International Airport, use the official taxi counter or a hotel pickup. Checking the fare in advance helps you avoid getting overcharged.
Clark is spread out and difficult to get around on foot. Install a ride-hailing app or consider a daily vehicle charter (about
For currency exchange, money changers inside malls generally offer better rates than the airport. ATMs are plentiful at large malls like SM Clark.
Sisig varies in style from restaurant to restaurant. Try comparing the traditional version without mayonnaise to the modern version topped with an egg.
The hot air balloon festival in
February
peaks around
6 AM
, when the balloons all rise together. Traffic control is heavy, so use a shuttle or set off early.
The lantern festival in San Fernando in
December
takes place at night and gets very crowded on weekends. Aim for a weekday evening instead.
It's convenient to split your schedule by time of day — malls and museums during the midday heat, and a walk on the Parade Ground in the late afternoon.
If you're planning a Pinatubo tour, arrive in Clark the evening before and get an early night. Pickup around
3–4 AM
is typical.
The area around Fields Avenue in Angeles is a nightlife district. Family travelers should avoid this area late at night, and always keep an eye on your belongings and drinks.
Prostitution is illegal in the Philippines and carries very heavy penalties. Don't respond to solicitation.
Some taxis try to negotiate a fare instead of running the meter. Prefer a ride-hailing app or hotel car.
At casinos, offers of gambling loans or being approached by strangers are likely to be scams.
Outdoor activity at midday during
March–May
carries a high risk of heatstroke. Drink water often and rest in the shade.
About
1–1.5 hours
by car. A popular day tour by 4x4 and trekking up to the emerald crater lake.
About
1 hour
by car (via SCTEX). A former U.S. naval base where you can enjoy jungle experiences, a marine theme park, and beaches.

1 hour
by car. A solitary dormant volcano rising from the Pampanga plain, with legends and trekking trails.

by car. A heritage resort in Bataan built from relocated old Philippine mansions.
